newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile could beat its '97 inflation target - Aninat.
newsitem.headline: Chile could beat its '97 inflation target - Aninat.

text.p: Chilean consumer inflation could end the year at 5.4 percent, a notch below the lowest official target of 5.5 percent, Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said.
"With a little luck in the rest of the year, and given that we don't see any pressure in the way of costs or spending, we could reach 5.4 percent," he told reporters.
Nonetheless, he said the government had no plans yet to change official inflation targets of 5.5-6.0 percent.
Consumer prices rose a tiny 0.2 percent in May, the smallest monthly increase since 1995, while year-on-year inflation was 5.4 percent, the lowest such figure in Chile's post-war history.
The May figure has practically guaranteed the 5.5 percent annual goal will be met, and preliminary targets for next year stand at about four percent, economists said.
